items.text: There is no version of this comparison where one side wins outright.
This is not a hedge against ambition.

blocks.heading: Test Before You Commit to Prep

items.text: Before you commit a year, let alone several, to a government exam attempt, run yourself honestly through The 3-Runway Test, the three practical questions that decide whether a multi-year attempt is a smart bet for your specific situation, not just an ambitious one.
Can your household genuinely absorb 1 to 3 years of zero or near-zero income without derailing rent, a sibling's education, or a parent's medical costs.

If the honest answer is "we would be in real financial trouble past year one," that is not a motivation problem, it is a runway problem, and it changes the decision regardless of how badly you want the post.

blocks.heading: How the Calculus Changes By Field

items.text: GATE-qualified PSU roles (NTPC, ONGC, BHEL, and similar) offer government-level security with meaningfully better starting pay than a typical Pay Level 1-6 clerical post, plus defined promotion timelines.

Bank PO exams (IBPS PO, SBI PO) run large annual vacancy cycles, IBPS PO alone opened over 6,700 posts and SBI PO around 1,500 posts in a recent cycle, with SBI PO cost-to-company revised upward to roughly Rs 21.97 lakh, making bank PO one of the better-paying, higher-volume government entry points for commerce graduates.

blocks.heading: Mistakes to Avoid When Making This Decision

items.text: The honest comparison changes completely by exam, by field, and by how much runway your specific household can absorb.
A private salary that looks higher often has real deductions once you price in bonus variability, notice-period risk, and no defined-benefit pension.
Termination requires proven serious misconduct, processed through formal departmental inquiries that commonly take years to resolve.
Work moves through defined channels and approvals, individual output rarely changes your monthly pay or promotion timeline.
Public holiday calendars typically run longer than private-sector norms, and leave policy is standardised and generous.

blocks.sourceSectionTitle: What actually differs, side by side

rows: Job security
Near-total. Termination requires proven serious misconduct, and the process runs through departmental inquiries and appeals that can take years.
Conditional on business performance. Layoffs happen during slowdowns, restructuring, or when a role becomes redundant, even at large stable companies.
Pay growth mechanism
Fixed annual increment of 3% of basic pay, plus a pay-commission revision roughly once a decade that resets the whole scale.
Performance-linked, with average appraisal hikes around 9.1% projected for 2026, and individual increments of 15-40% in fast-growing fields for strong performers.
Daily pace
Process-driven and rule-bound. Decisions move through defined channels; individual output rarely changes your monthly pay.
Output and deadline-driven. Targets, review cycles, and client or market pressure shape the day far more directly.
Time off and hours
Fixed hours, generous leave, and a public holiday calendar that typically runs noticeably longer than private-sector norms.
Hours track the role and sector; leave policy varies by company and is rarely as generous as the government holiday calendar.
entry requirement
A competitive written exam and, for many services, an interview, the exam itself is the main filter, not your resume.
Resume, interview rounds, and demonstrated skill or portfolio quality decide entry; no single national exam steps most private roles.

blocks.heading: 7th CPC Vs Private Salary Bands
blocks.sourceSectionTitle: Pay reality: 7th CPC vs private salary bands

rows: Entry level

Minimum basic pay across central government Pay Level 1 is Rs 18,000 a month under the 7th Pay Commission matrix. With Dearness Allowance at 60% (April 2026) and House Rent Allowance layered in, gross entry pay for a Level 1 post runs well above the basic figure, but most competitive-exam entrants land in Pay Level 6-10, which starts materially higher.

A fresh engineering graduate from a reasonable college typically starts around Rs 6-12 LPA in private tech roles; other fields vary widely by company tier, from services-company floors well below that to premium employers well above it.
Annual growth
Increments are fixed at 3% of basic pay each year, moving you one cell along your pay level in the matrix, regardless of individual performance.
Average projected appraisal hike for 2026 is 9.1%, with junior employees often seeing the highest increases as companies focus on retention; strong performers in high-demand skills can see far more.
Structural reset

Government pay does not track private-market inflation directly; it resets through pay commissions roughly once every ten years. The 7th CPC applied a 2.57 fitment factor in 2016, and an 8th Pay Commission was approved in principle in 2025, with a 25-34% hike under discussion, though terms of reference were still pending as of April 2026.

Private pay adjusts continuously through the job market, switching companies is the fastest lever, since internal appraisal caps rarely match what a competitive external offer can pay for the same skill.
